title: Global Load Balancing
description: Understand global load balancing, geo-routing, and how to serve users from the nearest data center while maintaining high availability.

data.text: Global load balancing extends traditional load balancing across multiple geographic regions. Instead of choosing a backend within a single data center, a global load balancer directs users to the nearest or healthiest region. This reduces latency, improves availability, and supports disaster recovery across regions.

Geo-routing uses the clients IP address or DNS resolver location to determine the optimal region. Users in Europe are routed to a European data center, while users in Asia are routed to an Asian data center. Many providers offer this through managed global load balancers such as Cloudflare Load Balancing or AWS Route 53 latency-based routing.

data.title: Tip
data.text: Geo-routing improves perceived performance because network latency is dominated by physical distance. Combine it with local load balancing for best results.

Global load balancers continuously monitor the health of regional endpoints. If a region becomes unhealthy, traffic is redirected to another region. This provides automatic failover without requiring users to change URLs or wait for DNS propagation delays if implemented at the DNS or proxy layer.

data.title: Key considerations
items: Data sovereignty and compliance may restrict which regions can store certain data.
Database replication lag affects read consistency across regions.
Failover behavior should be tested regularly because regional failures are rare and complex to simulate.

items.question: Does global load balancing require DNS changes?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Managed global load balancers can route traffic at the proxy layer while keeping a single endpoint. DNS-based options also work but may involve TTL delays.

items.question: How is global load balancing different from CDN routing?
items.answer: CDNs cache static content at edge locations. Global load balancing routes dynamic API and application traffic to regional data centers.

data.title: Takeaway
points: Global load balancing routes users to the nearest healthy region.
Geo-routing reduces latency and improves availability.
Combine global routing with local load balancing and robust health checks.
data.takeaway: Global load balancing is essential for low-latency, multi-region applications.
